name: Patricia Ramos
life: “I still remember belonging to a ride scheme where favors became overtime.” On Friday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Patricia knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I used to get lifts from my boss until I felt I couldn't refuse overtime. I want the rota to belong to the riders.
appearance: Patricia has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Look for dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a faded indigo overshirt with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. In conversation Patricia looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
personality: Patricia uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Patricia well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To get the rota into the riders' ownership.
family: August Jackson is Patricia’s older relative by marriage. Patricia gets to change the plan. August offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *A ship without postcards*, August says, “I fold the cards into boats. My granddaughter can open them only by reading flags.”
connections: Carol Dunn. One person wants a rider-owned rota. The other wants each rider to have a way out. Also in the story is Judith Dai (route planner).

reactions.situation: A shift worker is late to the meeting point
reactions.response: Patricia checks whether waiting will make the whole shift late and tells the rider the decision.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Patricia asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.
